title: Traffic Surgeon: automated rollback policies with multi-SLO tuning
creator: Priya Nair
description: Implement a production-safe automated rollback subsystem (Traffic Surgeon) that evaluates multiple SLO signals (latency p95, request error rate, token cost per 1k tokens, and throughput) and computes an adaptive composite rollback score per canary cohort. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect quality regressions while minimizing false positives that unnecessarily abort rollouts. This ticket covers the scoring algorithm, threshold tuning framework, runtime integration (proxy-level signal ingestion), and a Console UI for configuring per-project policies and viewing reasoned rollback decisions.
motivation: Current canary pipeline uses static thresholds per metric which either fires too late or causes noisy aborts when traffic mix shifts. We need a more robust, explainable mechanism that combines signals, supports per-cohort baselines, and auto-tunes thresholds based on historical distributions and safety budgets. Also add explicit token-cost awareness so teams can avoid expensive model variants silently inflating spend.
technical_approach: Introduce a composite rollback score computed as a weighted aggregation of normalized SLO deltas: latency_delta_norm, error_rate_delta_norm, cost_delta_norm, throughput_drop_norm
Baseline estimation: maintain rolling baseline per cohort using exp-weighted windows (7d for steady cohorts, 1d for volatile cohorts) with guardrails to avoid baseline poisoning during incidents
Adaptive thresholds: learn per-deployment thresholds using a percentile-based calibration (default 99th percentile of historical canary deltas) with gradient smoothing to avoid flapping
Statistical validation: use sequential hypothesis testing (alpha=0.01) with minimum sample sizes and bayesian credible intervals to reduce false positives on low-volume canaries
Cost-aware heuristics: compute token_cost_per_1k and include tunable penalty term to escalate rollback score for cost regressions even when latency/error are marginal

Runtime integration: implement a lightweight scoring service in the runtime-proxy path that ingests per-request metrics (latency, errors, tokens) and emits cohort-level aggregates to the control plane every 10s
Console: add Policy editor with sliders for per-metric weight, min_sample_size, detection_window, and a preview simulator that replays historical canaries
Fallbacks: allow automatic staged rollback (traffic 100->50->10->0) plus an option for immediate cutover and a manual abort interrupt
Observability: add rollback reason logs, per-cohort score time-series, and an incident dashboard linking to failing prompts/queries for evaluation
Safety mode: a conservative preset for enterprise customers that biases toward fewer false positives (higher sample sizes, longer windows)
acceptance_criteria: Scoring service implemented and deployed behind feature flag to canary runtime proxies
Runtime emits cohort-level aggregates every 10s and control plane stores time-series in TSDB
Console policy editor exists and can set weights + thresholds; changes take effect within 2m
At least three simulated historical canaries replayed through the simulator with expected rollback/no-rollback outcomes matching manual analysis
E2E test: when we inject a synthetic p95 latency increase of 30% and error spike to 1.5x baseline, Traffic Surgeon triggers staged rollback within configured detection_window
False-positive rate on low-traffic canaries <= 3% in 30-day A/B experiment with baseline policy
Token cost regressions detected and surfaced with clear cost delta and recommended action
PRs merged for runtime, control plane ingestion, and Console UI: runtime PR #1332, control-plane PR #1348, console PR #1407
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: baseline poisoning during incidents. Mitigation: use anomaly gating to suspend baseline updates when a global incident is detected
Risk: SLOs correlated with traffic mix changes (e.g., long-tail prompts). Mitigation: cohort by payload fingerprint and percentile-by-cohort baselines
Risk: increased control plane load from 10s aggregates. Mitigation: implement client-side downsampling and adaptive publish frequency based on traffic volume
Risk: teams disagree on weightings. Mitigation: provide sane presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and add policy preview with historical reprojections
implementation_notes: Use existing TSDB (metrics-db) for cohort time-series; schema: cohort_id, metric, timestamp, value
Scoring service will be written in Go, colocated with runtime-proxy; avoid blocking inference paths with async flushes
Add feature flag: feature.traffic_surgeon.enabled with rollout via Dedicated customers first
Telemetry: emit 'rollback_score' and 'rollback_decision' events to analytics topic for offline evaluation
Keep a human-readable 'reason' payload on rollback webhook: e.g., 'p95_latency +32% over baseline; token_cost +28% => composite score 0.82 > 0.75 threshold'
updates: 2025-11-03 Priya Nair: Ticket created. Initial proposal and toy scoring prototype evaluated on synthetic traces. Observed that token-cost signal often lags latency changes for batch jobs.

2025-11-06 Luis Ortega: Prototyped Go scoring lib and end-to-end trace replay harness. Added percentile calibration and sequential test skeleton. Found that minimum sample size of 200 requests per cohort reduces noise considerably.

2025-11-09 Design review (Maya Chen): Console policy editor mockups approved with feedback to show rollback rationale and a one-click 'pause rollouts' CTA. Action: DES-210 to add microcopy and accessibility checks.
2025-11-11 Eng sync: Decided on default weights (latency:0.4, errors:0.35, cost:0.15, throughput:0.1) and conservative preset. Action item: add A/B experiment to validate weights (ENG-56890).

2025-11-14 QA notes (Anita Gupta): Ran canary replay for three historical incidents. Traffic Surgeon matched manual outcome in 2/3; in one case it was slower to trigger due to low sample volume. QA recommends a min_sample_size override per-project.
2025-11-16 Release lead (Carlos Mendes): Feature flag gating agreed. Targeting Dedicated customers first; will enable host-level telemetry retention for 30d before broader release.

2025-11-18 Luis Ortega: Runtime PR #1332 opened (link above). Control-plane ingestion stub PR #1348 opened. Console skeleton PR #1407 opened. Adding 2-sprint follow-up for policy templates and per-cohort baselining improvements.
